title: Koszul orthogonality detects extension from an open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let j:U \to X be an open immersion, let V=Spec(A) be an affine open of X, and suppose X=U union V with U intersection V quasi-compact. Put Z=V minus U, choose f_1, ..., f_r in A with Z=V(f_1, ..., f_r), and let K be the bounded Koszul complex whose degree-q term is the q-th exterior power of A^r and whose differential is contraction with (f_1, ..., f_r), viewed as a perfect object of D(O_V) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every E in D_QCoh(O_V) [def-pc-derived-category], the following are equivalent: (i) the canonical map E \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) is an isomorphism; (ii) Hom(K[n],E)=0 for every integer n.

proof.text: Let C be the cone of the canonical map E \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V). The restriction of K to U intersection V is zero (Elementary, Stacks Tag 0663: multiplication by each f_i is homotopic to zero on K, so on each D(f_i), where f_i is a unit, K is acyclic; the D(f_i) cover U intersection V=V minus V(f_1, ..., f_r).), so derived adjunction gives Hom(K[n], R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V))=0 for every n. Applying Hom(K[n],-) to the distinguished triangle E \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) \to C \to E[1] therefore shows that Hom(K[n],E)=0 for all n if and only if Hom(K[n],C)=0 for all n. The canonical map is an isomorphism exactly when C=0.

source.place: Tag 09IR, proof: distinguished triangle and vanishing after restricting the Koszul complex to U

proof.text: The cone C restricts to zero on U intersection V, since the canonical map restricts there to an isomorphism (elementary: restriction to an open is exact and the restriction of R(U intersection V \to V)_* to U intersection V is computed on an injective resolution as the identity, Stacks Tag 08DF-type compatibility). On the affine V=Spec(A), the closed complement V minus U is V(f_1, ..., f_r). The Koszul multiplication triangles (elementary, Stacks Tag 062C: K(..., f g, ...) is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a map K(..., f, ...)[1] \to K(..., g, ...), giving a distinguished triangle in D(O_V)) give, for each coordinate i and positive a,b, a distinguished triangle whose three terms are the Koszul complexes with exponents a, b, and a+b in that coordinate (and with the other exponents fixed). Applying Hom(-,C) yields a long exact sequence. Starting with the exponent tuple (1,...,1), induction on the sum of the exponents therefore shows that vanishing of Hom(K[n],C) for all n implies vanishing for every positive power tuple: to increase one exponent from m to m+1, use the triangle with a=m and b=1, whose other two Koszul terms have smaller sums. The auxiliary affine Koszul detection statement [lem-pc-koszul-affine-detection] now applies to C and gives C=0. Hence Hom(K[n],E)=0 for all n implies that the canonical map in (i) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09IR, proof using Lemma 36.9.6 and Lemma 36.3.5

proof.text: Conversely, if the canonical map E \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) is an isomorphism, then E is identified with that derived pushforward. Since K restricts to zero on U intersection V (Step 1, Stacks Tag 0663), derived adjunction gives Hom(K[n],E)=0 for every integer n.
